title: Create Hello World Function
interviewTips: Ask whether the returned function must ignore all arguments and always return exactly "Hello World" with that casing and spacing?
Trade-off to discuss: explicit named inner function is more readable and stack-trace friendly vs concise lambda which is shorter but equivalent in O(1) time and space.
Confirm testing expectations: multiple invocations, calls with zero / many / varied-type args, and strict equality check on the returned string.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Closure with Named Inner Function
approaches.intuition: We need a factory that makes a function. Create an outer function that defines and returns a separate named inner function which always returns the constant string "Hello World" regardless of inputs.
approaches.theory: This relies on first-class functions and lexical closure. The inner function closes over its defining scope but needs no captured variables since the return value is a constant. The outer factory does O(1) work to allocate and return the function object; each invocation of the returned function does O(1) work to return a constant string. No loops or extra state are needed.

timeComplexity.explanation: Factory creates one function object in constant time; each call of the returned function returns a constant string in constant time.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only one function object and one constant string are allocated; no input-dependent storage.

steps: Call createHelloWorld() -> defines inner function and returns its reference as f
Call f() with no args -> inner executes and returns "Hello World"
Call f({}, null, 123) with extra args -> args are ignored (*args/**kwargs or ...args) and still returns "Hello World"

edgeCases: No arguments: f() must still return "Hello World"
Extra arguments of any type/count: f(1,2,3), f(null, {}, "x") must be ignored
Multiple calls on same returned function must consistently return same string
Exact string match: case, space, and no trailing newline required

approaches.name: Approach 2: Optimal Concise Lambda Factory
approaches.intuition: The named inner function is boilerplate. Directly return an anonymous lambda / arrow function that ignores its rest parameters and returns "Hello World" — same behavior with minimal code.
approaches.theory: Identical closure semantics but using lambda expression syntax. In JS: () => "Hello World" or (...args) => "Hello World". In Python: lambda *args, **kwargs: "Hello World". In C++: [](){ return "Hello World"; }. In Java: () -> "Hello World". The lambda is a function value created in O(1) time that captures nothing and returns a constant, so time and space remain O(1) with less indirection.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single lambda allocation on factory call and constant-time return on each invocation; no iteration over arguments.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only the lambda/closure object is stored; it captures no variables so overhead is constant.

steps: Call createHelloWorld() -> directly returns lambda () => "Hello World" as f
Call f("a", "b") -> rest args collected but unused, returns "Hello World"
Call f() again -> still returns "Hello World", proving stateless idempotence

edgeCases: Variadic calls: function must accept ...args / *args to avoid arity errors in JS/Python
Repeated factory calls: createHelloWorld() twice should give independent but equivalent functions
Strict equality: return must be primitive string "Hello World", not String object or with extra whitespace
No side effects: lambda must not mutate external state or depend on closure variables
